# Critical chord geometry controls the section weights

This is a planar structural consequence of actual zero-endpoint
criticality. It gives an automatic contraction criterion when all three
unique-capture regions of the contracted endpoint are absent. It does
not assert that this residual pattern must occur, nor does it discard
the possible equality of an endpoint depth with the global depth.

## 1. The actual geometric hypotheses and normalized sections

Let A,K,B be planar convex bodies at the three integer bases -1,0,1,
with (A+B)/2 contained in K. These are the only integer fibers. Let
y be in the interior of K, and let the nonzero spanning normals
v_1,v_2,v_3 have v_1+v_2+v_3=0. Set h_i=h_B(v_i).

Assume each of the actual caps

    v_i.(x-y)+(v_i.y-h_i)z >= 0

is depth-attaining at (0,y), and its cuts on A and K are proper.
Its B trace is the supporting face F_i=B intersect {v_i.x=h_i}
and has zero area. Put

    b_i=2v_i.y-h_i,
    a_i=H_1(A intersect {v_i.x=b_i})/||v_i||,
    k_i=H_1(K intersect {v_i.x=v_i.y})/||v_i||,
    s_i=2a_i+k_i, lambda_i=1/s_i, Lambda=sum lambda_i.

All a_i,k_i are positive. Genuine criticality forces a positive-length
supporting B face. The full facet first-variation condition and actual
midpoint inclusion imply the chord-center inequality proved in Section 4
of `candidate 6ac02348e3ceb9a9`.
The elementary consequence needed here is restated and proved below,
so the use of lengths divided by ||v_i|| is explicit.

Let J be a Euclidean rotation through a right angle. Parametrize the
middle cutting line by x=y+t Jv_i. Its Euclidean arclength differential
is ||v_i|| dt, so its length in t is exactly k_i. The A and B parallel
cutting lines can be given compatible t coordinates by translating their
origins so that the midpoint of the A and B origins is y. Write c_A,c_K
for their interval-center coordinates, and let c_B be the center of F_i
in this same compatible coordinate. The middle center is measured from
y, so c_K is its signed displacement from the source.

Write f_i=H_1(F_i)/||v_i||. The critical facet moment condition says
that the interval F_i contains a subinterval of length a_i whose center
is

    c_*=-c_A-(k_i/a_i)c_K.

This is exactly the fixed-mass moment interval of an actual interval;
its possible means range between the centers of its leftmost and
rightmost length-a_i subintervals. Taking the midpoint sum of the A
section and that B subinterval gives a middle subinterval of length a_i
with center -(k_i/(2a_i))c_K. Its containment in the K cutting interval
therefore implies

    |c_K| <= a_i(k_i-a_i)/(k_i+2a_i),   k_i>=a_i.       (1)

This repeats the proved critical-chord argument using t coordinates.
It uses neither an independently chosen B facet center nor a free
moment assignment.

## 2. A symmetric gauge gives an exact section-weight bound

Define the actual centrally symmetric convex body

    D=(K-y) intersect -(K-y).

It has nonempty interior because y is interior to K. Its Minkowski
gauge N is a norm: positive homogeneity and symmetry are immediate,
and if x in alpha D, z in beta D, convexity gives
x+z in (alpha+beta)D. Taking infima proves the triangle inequality.

Let rho_i be the positive radial parameter of D along Jv_i. It equals
the smaller of the two t-distances from y to the endpoints of the
actual K cutting chord. Therefore (1) gives

    rho_i = k_i/2-|c_K|
       >= (k_i^2+2a_i^2)/(2(k_i+2a_i))
       >= (k_i+2a_i)/6 = s_i/6.                       (2)

The second inequality is exactly

    3(k_i^2+2a_i^2)-(k_i+2a_i)^2
       =2(k_i-a_i)^2 >=0.

Also rho_i<=k_i/2<=s_i/2. Thus

    2lambda_i <= N(Jv_i)=1/rho_i <=6lambda_i.          (3)

Since Jv_1+Jv_2+Jv_3=0, symmetry and the triangle inequality of this
ONE actual norm imply

    2lambda_i <= N(Jv_i)
       <= N(Jv_j)+N(Jv_l) <=6(lambda_j+lambda_l).

Consequently

    lambda_i <=3(lambda_j+lambda_l),
    max_i lambda_i/Lambda <=3/4.                     (4)

This is a proved restriction on the actual section weights. No claim
that the constant 3 is sharp for full mixed critical configurations is
needed or made.

## 3. Empty unique-capture regions give automatic shell credit

Write H_i^A={x:v_i.x>=b_i} and define

    R_i=A intersect intersection_(j!=i){x:v_j.x<b_j}.

The three A halfspaces cover the plane. Indeed sum b_i=-sum h_i<0:
an interior point of B has each h_i strictly larger than v_i evaluated
there, and their sum is strictly positive. A point missing all three
A halfspaces would give 0=sum v_i.x<sum b_i<0.

Suppose every R_i is empty, or more generally has zero area. Except
on a null set, every point of A is then captured by at least two of
the three A halfspaces. Since all lambda_i are positive, its weighted
capture load is at least

    tau=Lambda-max_i lambda_i >= Lambda/4.            (5)

Fix ANY actual contraction center p in A and set
A_t=p+(1-t)(A-p). It is a nested subset of A. With
U_i=|A intersect H_i^A|, the removed i-cap volume is exactly the
measure of (A minus A_t) intersect H_i^A. Integrating (5) on this
actual removed shell gives

    sum_i lambda_i[U_i-|A_t intersect H_i^A|]
       >= (Lambda/4)[a-|A_t|],  a=|A|.

Each proper cut has continuous section length as a function of its
threshold. Differentiating the exact homothety cap formula at t=0
therefore gives

    L_i(p)=2U_i+(b_i-v_i.p)a_i,
    sum_i lambda_i L_i(p) >= Lambda a/2.              (6)

The same p is used in every cap. The conclusion holds for EVERY p in
A, including boundary centers. It is stronger in this residual pattern
than a criterion requiring the three section weights to be comparable.

## 4. Precisely scoped finite-menu descent

Apply `candidate 0e094dd9f76aefdd`.
Its actual implicit meeting-point construction has common menu budget
q(t), with q(0)=Q and

    q'(0)=-Lbar(p),
    Lbar(p)=sum lambda_i L_i(p)/Lambda >=a/2.

Assume additionally that Q is the original globally maximal raw mixed
depth, that both endpoint ordinary maximal depths are STRICTLY below Q,
and that Q/M<2/9, where M=a+|K|+|B|. The endpoint gaps persist for
sufficiently small contractions. The actual maximum new raw depth is
bounded by q(t), while M'(0)=-2a. Hence the derivative of its normalized
upper certificate at zero satisfies

    [q(t)/M(t)]'_(t=0)
       <=[-M a/2+2aQ]/M^2
       < -a/(18M) <0.                               (7)

Thus this actual nested body deformation strictly lowers the optimized
normalized depth. The displayed caps need not remain minimizing after
the deformation. This is a valid descent obstruction to an attained
below-target local minimum under the stated strict endpoint gaps; it is
not a proof that every below-target body has this residual pattern or
these gaps. A tied endpoint must be treated with the separate two-rate
certificate in the cited source.

There is a scope distinction in the specifically planar B-nonheavy
bad-source regime studied in the small-endpoint note. Its already
proved profile bound a-u-v>=w/4>0 forces the largest-cap unique corner
to be present. Thus the all-empty-corner specialization above is not
an additional direct OC exclusion beyond that profile. The gauge
restriction (4) remains an independent constraint in every residual
pattern and shows that pair-capture regions themselves have sufficient
weight; deficient PRESENT singleton regions are the remaining issue.

## 5. The elementary shell argument in every dimension

For reference, its incidence part is independent of the planar gauge
argument. Let A be a d-dimensional convex body, and let finitely many
closed halfspaces H_i cover A. For positive weights w_i and any tau
such that sum_(i:x in H_i)w_i>=tau almost everywhere on A, integration
over every actual homothetic removed shell gives

    sum_i w_i L_i(p)>=d a tau for every p in A,
    L_i(p)=d|A intersect H_i|+(b_i-v_i.p)sigma_i,

provided the cuts are proper and sigma_i is their normalized
(d-1)-section area. The derivative follows from the same homothety
formula and interior continuity of convex section volumes.

If the only known incidences are absence of singleton-capture regions
indexed by E, one may take

    tau=min({w_i:i notin E} union {w_i+w_j:i!=j}),

omitting an empty singleton list. Every nonempty capture set is either
an allowed singleton or contains a pair, and all weights are positive.
This proves the exact absence/multiplicity load used in the planar
contraction source. Only Sections 1--4 above use two-dimensional chord
and norm geometry; no all-dimensional analogue of (4) is asserted.

## 6. One small present corner can be charged at its own center

Continue in the planar geometric setting of Sections 1--2, and put
tau_2=Lambda-max lambda_i, the minimum pair weight. At every A point,
the weighted capture load is at least tau_2 unless the point belongs
to a singleton-capture region R_i with lambda_i<tau_2. Precisely,

    capture_load(x) >= tau_2
       -sum_i(tau_2-lambda_i)_+ 1_(R_i)(x).           (8)

Assume at most ONE deficient region (lambda_i<tau_2) has positive
area, and denote its index by j. Choose any actual p in the closure of
R_j, a nonempty subset of A. For x in R_j and 0<=t<1, every defining
missed inequality is weak at p and strict at x, so

    p+(1-t)(R_j-p) subset A_t intersect R_j,
    |R_j minus A_t| <=[1-(1-t)^2]|R_j|.              (9)

Integrate (8) on A minus A_t, use (9), divide by t, and let t decrease
to zero. The proper original cap derivatives give

    Lbar(p) >=
       [2a tau_2-2(tau_2-lambda_j)|R_j|]/Lambda.      (10)

If every deficient region is null, the subtracted term vanishes and
any p works. Since tau_2>=Lambda/4, a useful sufficient condition is

    |R_j|<=a/9  ==>  Lbar(p)>=4a/9.                 (11)

Indeed (10) is at least (a-|R_j|)/2. Under the global-Q,
strict-endpoint-gap, and Q/M<2/9 assumptions of Section 4, this gives
actual strict normalized descent. No incompatible contraction centers
for two different corners have been combined.

## 7. Exact removable-corner loss and an attained common-center reserve

The corner loss in (10) can be computed exactly from actual facets.
Fix i, with remaining indices j,l, and assume r_i=|R_i|>0. Let

    tau_ij=H_1(A intersect {v_j.x=b_j, v_l.x<=b_l})/||v_j||,
    tau_il=H_1(A intersect {v_l.x=b_l, v_j.x<=b_j})/||v_l||.

These numbers may vanish. All the ORIGINAL cuts on A are proper.
For every p in A the removed-corner derivative exists and is

    D_i(p)=lim_(t down to0) |R_i minus A_t|/t
       =2r_i-sum_(j!=i)(b_j-v_j.p)tau_ij.            (12)

Here the corner is fixed while A contracts. In particular D_i(p)>=0.
If p is in the closure of R_i, all the displayed distances b_j-v_j.p
are nonnegative and D_i(p)<=2r_i, recovering (9).

For a direct proof, pull the moving A_t back to A. Its corner
thresholds become

    b_j(t)=(b_j-t v_j.p)/(1-t)
          =b_j+t(b_j-v_j.p)+O(t^2).

The area cut from A by the two moving inequalities is differentiable
at this threshold pair, with respective partial derivatives tau_ij
and tau_il. To justify this without regularity assumptions on the
boundary of A, integrate the added or removed thin strip parallel to
one cut line. The other cut indicator changes only at its single
intersection point with that line. Because the original A cut is
proper, the boundary of A on that line consists of its two interval
endpoints; all other line points are either interior or exterior.
Thus bounded convergence in the tangential coordinate gives the
stated strip derivative. All relevant tangential coordinates stay in
one bounded interval because A is compact. The intersection of the
two changed strips has area O(t^2): the two normals are independent,
so the linear coordinate map x->(v_j.x,v_l.x) has a nonzero constant
Jacobian. This also handles opposite signs of their threshold changes.
Multiplication by the area factor (1-t)^2 proves (12).

The closure C_i of R_i equals A intersect {v_j.x<=b_j, v_l.x<=b_l}:
since r_i>0 there is a point of int A satisfying both strict
inequalities, and mixing that point with any point of the closed
intersection proves the claimed density. Therefore C_i is compact,
and minimizing (12) over C_i is an attained support problem:

    min_(p in C_i)D_i(p)
       =2r_i-sum_(j!=i)b_j tau_ij
          -h_(C_i)(-sum_(j!=i)tau_ij v_j).           (13)

This can be strictly smaller than 2r_i, and it uses the original
facets of the actual corner. In a corner that is locally a cone with
apex p, its two sloping A boundaries are invariant under homothety
about p, and (12) can be zero even when r_i>0.

There is also a simultaneous version with one common center for
several deficient corners. Write c_i=(tau_2-lambda_i)_+. Ignore null
corners, whose intersections with every removed shell are null.
Integration of (8) and (12) gives for EVERY p in A

    sum lambda_i L_i(p) >=2a tau_2-sum_i c_i D_i(p).

The right side is affine in p. It has an attained maximum over the
same actual body A, with value

    2a tau_2-2sum_i c_i r_i
      +sum_i c_i sum_(j!=i)b_j tau_ij
      +h_A(-sum_i c_i sum_(j!=i)tau_ij v_j).          (14)

Thus (14) is a proved common-center improvement even when two
deficient corners are present. It does not presume that the separate
minimizers from (13) coincide. The previously omitted extra weights on
some pair-capture and triple-capture regions are nonnegative; dropping
them is the only incidence loss in deriving (14). No automatic lower
bound sufficient for descent is inferred from (14) without an actual
geometric estimate of its displayed quantities.
